label: Kitchens

sections.label: What we plan with you
sections.title: The details that make the difference.

items.name: Layout
items.text: Where you prep, cook, clean and sit, and how people move through the room.

items.name: Cabinetry and storage
items.text: A place for everything you use, sized to the room.

items.name: Surfaces
items.text: Counters, flooring and finishes chosen for looks and for daily use.

items.name: Lighting and fixtures
items.text: Task light where you work. Atmosphere where you sit.

sections.label: Scope first
sections.alt: Completed kitchen with a waterfall island and range hood
sections.title: Keep the layout, or change everything.
text: They are different projects. We agree the scope with you before anything is built, so the estimate matches the work.

items.q: Do I need a design before contacting you?
items.a: No. Tell us what you want to change, and share drawings or inspiration if you have them.

items.q: Can I keep the existing layout?
items.a: Yes. If the layout already works, the project can focus on cabinetry, surfaces, fixtures and finishes.

items.q: What affects the cost?
items.a: The size and condition of the room, layout changes, cabinetry, appliances and finishes. We prepare an estimate once the scope is defined.

items.q: How long will the renovation take?
items.a: It depends on the scope, permits where needed, your selections and material lead times. Tell us about any important dates at the start.

label: Bathrooms

items.name: Layout
items.text: Fixture positions, floor space and the way doors open.

items.name: Shower and bath
items.text: Arranged for comfort, easy cleaning and the people who use it.

items.name: Storage and lighting
items.text: Everyday items within reach. Light suited to the task.

items.name: What’s behind the walls
items.text: Plumbing, ventilation and waterproofing, planned with the finishes.

sections.label: Any size
sections.alt: Completed bathroom with marble tile and a double vanity
sections.title: A powder room or a primary suite.
text: We take single bathrooms and bathrooms within a larger renovation. If it is the only one in the home, we plan access during the work with you.

items.q: Can you work on a small bathroom?
items.a: Yes. We welcome smaller bathroom projects as well as larger renovations.

items.q: Can the bathroom layout change?
items.a: Often. It depends on the building, the plumbing and the space available. Share your goals and we will review the options.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom easier to access?
items.a: Tell us about the access and comfort needs you want the project to address, and we will assess what suits your home.

items.q: Can a bathroom be part of a whole-home renovation?
items.a: Yes. Planning it with the other rooms keeps the work and the decisions coordinated.

items.q: Does the entire house have to be renovated at once?
items.a: No. The work can sometimes be phased, depending on the scope and how the parts of the project connect.

items.q: Can I live at home during the work?
items.a: It depends on the areas affected, essential services and safety. We discuss it with you early.

items.q: What should I bring to the first enquiry?

sections.title: Built to belong.
text: An addition often changes the rooms beside it. We scope both together, so the new space connects properly with your home.

items.q: Can you tell me whether an addition is possible from a message?
items.a: We can take the first details and tell you what needs review. Feasibility is confirmed with property and planning information.

items.q: Do additions require permits?
items.a: Permit and planning requirements depend on the location and scope. We check them for your project before work proceeds.

items.q: Can an addition include remodeling existing rooms?
items.a: Yes. Tell us about the new space and the rooms you want to change, and we will plan them together.

text: Where the property is, whether water is coming in, and where it shows. Photos taken from the ground help. Please don’t climb onto the roof.

items.q: How do I know whether to repair or replace the roof?
items.a: It depends on the roof’s condition and the extent of the damage. We assess the roof before recommending either.

items.q: Can I send photographs?
items.a: Yes. Email them to info@isdesignandbuild.com. Use photographs you can take safely from the ground.

items.q: Do you offer emergency service?
items.a: Call (202) 519-1831 about anything urgent and we will confirm availability.

items.q: What roof materials do you work with?
items.a: Tell us what you know about your existing roof, or choose “Not sure” in the enquiry. We confirm the right system for your home.

items.q: What services do you offer?
items.a: Kitchen and bathroom remodeling, whole-home renovations, home additions and roofing. If your project includes something else, describe it in your enquiry.

items.q: Do you take smaller projects?
items.a: Yes. We welcome single-room projects as well as substantial renovations.

items.q: Where do you work?
items.a: Washington, DC, Northern Virginia and Montgomery County, Maryland, including Bethesda and Chevy Chase. Share your town or ZIP code to confirm coverage.

items.q: Do I need drawings before contacting you?

items.q: Can you give me a price online?

items.q: How do I speak to someone?

items.q: Do I have to use financing?
items.a: No. It is one way to pay. We discuss payment when the scope and estimate are prepared.

items.q: How are rates and payments set?
items.a: By the lender, based on the loan and your circumstances. Read the lender’s terms before you commit, and compare more than one offer.

items.q: Does applying commit me to a project?
items.a: No. Applying to a lender is separate from agreeing a project with us. Ask the lender how an application affects you.

items.q: Can I finance roofing work?
items.a: Ask the lender whether the work qualifies. Eligibility is the lender’s decision.

title: Lead Paint in Older DC Homes | I.S Design + Build
description: Planning work on a home built before 1978? Tell us what you know about lead paint so it can be considered in the scope from the start.
label: Lead paint
headline: Older home? Plan for lead paint early.
lede: Many Washington, DC homes were built before 1978, when lead-based paint was still in use.

sections.label: Why it matters
sections.title: Old paint becomes dust.
text: Sanding, cutting and demolition release it. Lead dust is harmful, especially to young children and during pregnancy. The EPA sets rules for renovation work in pre-1978 homes.

link.text: Read the EPA’s guidance on lead

sections.label: What to tell us
sections.title: Raise it at the start.

items.name: The home
items.text: Its age, and any inspection or risk-assessment reports you have.

items.name: The work
items.text: Which rooms and surfaces are affected, and whether paint is peeling.

items.name: The household
items.text: Young children or anyone pregnant living in the home.

sections.note: Raising it early keeps containment, dust control and clean-up inside the scope and the estimate. Lead inspections and risk assessments are carried out by a licensed inspector or risk assessor.

items.q: How do I know whether my home has lead paint?
items.a: The age of the home is the first sign. Only testing by a qualified professional can confirm it. Do not sand or scrape paint to find out.

items.q: Can I stay at home during the work?
items.a: It depends on the areas affected and how they can be separated from the rest of the home. We discuss it before work is scheduled.

items.q: Is this a separate project?
items.a: It can be part of a renovation or a request on its own. Describe what you need in your enquiry.
